definitions.explanation: The act of striking one's palms together to show appreciation or approval.

examples.japanese: {観客|かんきゃく}から{大|おお}きな{拍手|はくしゅ}が{起|お}こった。
examples.english: There was loud applause from the audience.
examples.notes: 拍手が起こる = applause breaks out

examples.japanese: {演奏|えんそう}が{終|お}わると、{拍手|はくしゅ}が{鳴|な}り{止|や}まなかった。
examples.english: When the performance ended, the applause wouldn't stop.

examples.japanese: {皆|みな}さん、{拍手|はくしゅ}をお{願|ねが}いします。
examples.english: Everyone, please give a round of applause.

examples.japanese: {拍手|はくしゅ}で{迎|むか}えられた。
{彼|かれ}のスピーチが{終|お}わると、{会場|かいじょう}{全体|ぜんたい}からスタンディングオベーションと{割|わ}れんばかりの{拍手|はくしゅ}が{送|おく}られた。
examples.english: When his speech ended, there was a standing ovation and thunderous applause from the entire venue.
examples.notes: {割|わ}れんばかりの{拍手|はくしゅ} = deafening applause

notes:
USAGE: {拍手|はくしゅ} is used for clapping as a sign of appreciation. Note that clapping at shrines ({拍手|かしわで}) uses a different reading.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{拍手|はくしゅ}する (to clap, to applaud)
・{拍手|はくしゅ}を{送|おく}る (to give applause)
・{拍手|はくしゅ}{喝采|かっさい} (applause and cheers)
・{万雷|ばんらい}の{拍手|はくしゅ} (thunderous applause)
・{拍手|はくしゅ}が{鳴|な}り{響|ひび}く (applause resounds)

TYPES OF APPLAUSE:
・スタンディングオベーション (standing ovation)
・アンコールの{拍手|はくしゅ} (encore applause)

NOTE: At Shinto shrines, ritual clapping is read as {拍手|かしわで} or {柏手|かしわで}.
